nodes.summary: For every list $xs$ over a linearly ordered type, the simultaneous minimum and maximum algorithm returns no result on $xs$ if and only if $xs$ is empty.
nodes.title: The min–max algorithm returns no result exactly on the empty list

nodes.summary: For every list $xs$ over a linearly ordered type and all elements $lo$ and $hi$ of that type, the simultaneous minimum and maximum algorithm returns the pair $(lo, hi)$ on $xs$ if and only if $lo$ and $hi$ both belong to $xs$, $lo \le x$ for every $x$ in $xs$, and $x \le hi$ for every $x$ in $xs$.
nodes.title: Characterization of the min–max output

nodes.summary: On the empty list, the simultaneous minimum and maximum algorithm returns no result and makes no comparisons.
nodes.title: The min–max algorithm on the empty list

nodes.summary: For every list $xs$ over a linearly ordered type, the simultaneous minimum and maximum algorithm returns no result on $xs$ when $xs$ is empty, and returns the pair $(\min xs, \max xs)$ of the least and greatest elements of $xs$ otherwise.
nodes.title: Correctness of the simultaneous minimum and maximum algorithm

nodes.summary: For every element $a$ of a linearly ordered type, on the list $[a]$ the simultaneous minimum and maximum algorithm returns the pair $(a, a)$ and makes no comparisons.
nodes.title: The min–max algorithm on a one-element list

nodes.summary: For every natural number $k \ge 1$ and every list of length $2k$ over a linearly ordered type, the simultaneous minimum and maximum algorithm makes exactly $3k - 2$ comparisons.
nodes.title: Comparisons of the min–max algorithm on even-length lists

nodes.summary: For every natural number $k$ and every list of length $2k + 1$ over a linearly ordered type, the simultaneous minimum and maximum algorithm makes exactly $3k$ comparisons.
nodes.title: Comparisons of the min–max algorithm on odd-length lists

nodes.summary: For every list of length $n$ over a linearly ordered type, the simultaneous minimum and maximum algorithm makes no comparisons when $n = 0$ and exactly $\lceil 3n/2 \rceil - 2$ comparisons when $n \ge 1$.
nodes.title: Comparison count of the simultaneous minimum and maximum algorithm

nodes.summary: Given a list $xs$ over a linearly ordered type, the paired algorithm returns no result when $xs$ is empty and otherwise returns a pair (a candidate minimum and a candidate maximum), counting one unit of time for each comparison of elements. can_prove.label: ready to prove
can_prove.meaning: Statement is in Lean and nothing it needs is blocked, so the proof can start.

can_state.label: ready to state
can_state.meaning: Everything its statement uses is in Lean, so the statement can be written in Lean.

conditional.label: conditionally proved
conditional.meaning: Proof compiles, but rests on an open statement without a recorded Lean proof.

fully_proved.label: fully proved
fully_proved.meaning: Proved, and every prerequisite is fully proved too.

inventory_checked.label: inventory checked
inventory_checked.meaning: Module inventory checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

inventory_pending.label: inventory pending
inventory_pending.meaning: Module inventory not yet checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

not_ready.label: not ready
not_ready.meaning: Needs more blueprint work before it can be attempted.

proved.label: proved
proved.meaning: Proof compiles, but something it rests on is not finished.

stated.label: statement formalized
stated.meaning: Statement is in Lean; the proof is not.
